main_text.p: „ mihi ex sententia debebi-tur, „ quia ego uicero: Sin uerò se-„ cundum te iudicatum erit, „ merces mihi ex pacto debebi-„ tur, quia tu uiceris. Ad ea re-„ spondit Euathlus: Potui, in-„ quit, huic tuae tam ancipiti „ captioni ille obuiam, si uer-„ ba non ipse facerem, sed alio „ patrono uterer. sed magis mi-„ hi in ista uictoria proludium „ est, cum te nō in causa tantū, „ sed in argumento quoque i-„ sto uinco. Disce igitur tu quo-„ que magister sapientissime, „ utroque modo fieri, ut non „ reddam quod petis: siue con-„ tra me pronunciatū fuerit, si-„ ue pro me. Nā si iudices pro „ cau-

page.notes: Each line of the text begins with a printed opening quotation mark („), transcribed as shown. The long s is printed as a plain s throughout. "sapientissime" has an accent over the second i, shown as printed, and the printer's "ss" is read as ss. The running head at top right is too faded to read reliably. Line-end hyphens are kept as printed. The "f" in "Disce" was read as the printed long-s form in the scan.
